name: Open Stacks
description: A research wiki on exploring the world's literature cheaply and well: what is free and legal (open-access books and papers, public domain), cheap and institutional access routes (subscriptions, public and university libraries), discovery and AI research tools, reading environments from e-ink to VR, the legal constraints on building tools, a reference architecture for a personal catalog of everything, and a gallery of interface mockups and prototypes. Maintained by QURI (quantifieduncertainty.org) as part of the CAIRN project. Every page is a dated working draft; prices and product statuses are as of October 2026.
intro: The organizing idea: separate the catalog (titles, tables of contents, summaries, topic placement: small, mostly open data) from the content (scattered across open repositories, libraries, subscriptions and paywalls), then build one place to browse everything that routes each work to wherever it can actually be read, at the right page. Sibling wikis: Robust Reasoning Processes (https://reasoning-processes.quantifieduncertainty.org) and Evaluation Engineering (https://evaluation-engineering.quantifieduncertainty.org).
